newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Brent prompt futures extend 5-yr highs on SIMEX.
newsitem.headline: Brent prompt futures extend 5-yr highs on SIMEX.

text.p: SIMEX Brent front-month futures extended gains early afternoon on Wednesday, pushed by worries over low U.S. heating oil stocks and buying by a European major.

November was last traded at the intraday high of $25.15 per barrel, up 42 cents from the London close on Tuesday of $24.73. December Brent was last traded at $24.42, up 31 cents from London's close and just off the intraday high of $24.48. Market volume was 211 lots.
Brokers said overnight stock data supported the market.

American Petroleum Institute (API) data after NYMEX closed on Tuesday showed distillate stocks rose a less-than-expected 673,000 barrels to 114.3 million barrels. But more significantly, stocks fell in the northeast, the biggest heating oil market in the world.
Brokers said a European major was a noted buyer of Brent futures, which they attributed to buying ahead of the November expiry later on Wednesday in London.
